type:
∀ (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [Ring A] [Ring B]
  (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u z} A) (ModuleCat.{w} B))
  [CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F],
  let regular := ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{z} A)
  let lift := LinearEquiv.symm (ULift.moduleEquiv : ULift.{z} A ≃ₗ[A] A)
  let M := CategoryTheory.Functor.obj F regular
  ∃ N : Bimodule.1 B A M,
    N.1 = ModuleCat.isModule M ∧
    ∀ (a : A) (m : M),
      @SMul.smul (MulOpposite A) M
        N.2.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul (MulOpposite.op a) m =
      ModuleCat.Hom.hom
        (CategoryTheory.Functor.map F
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearEquiv.conjRingEquiv lift (LinearMap.mulRight A a)))) m
sourceReason:
The plan designates the statement from Alphabeta Math, F(A) is a (B,A)-bimodule for every additive functor F (lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action), as the endpoint. https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action

ULift represents the regular left A-module in the source carrier universe and transports right multiplication to that representative. The Lean check constructed the specified bimodule without choice. The defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, so its contents could not be reviewed. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
